analysis.title: Assessing AI Risk in Loans
key_insights: MS adapts the equity team's Moat & Journey framework and uses AI-powered research tools to score 131 software leveraged loan issuers. By outstanding par, 16% of software loans are Red (high AI risk), 49% Amber and 35% Green. The universe is about $250bn of software loans.

Red exposure overlaps with credit weakness. About 72% ($26bn) of the $37bn rated Red cohort is rated B- or lower. Red loans are about 40% of the $37bn CCC-rated cohort, versus 7% of BB and 11% of B. No Green loans sit in the CCC cohort.

AI risk is reflected in loan prices. Weighted-average bids as of Oct. 29 are 97 for Green, 88 for Amber and 73 for Red. A 10-point rise in the AI risk score is associated with about a 5-point lower loan price, controlling for rating and maturity. Adding the score lifts adjusted R-squared by 4-6pp.

Price dispersion widens with AI risk. The interquartile range is 3 points for Green, 13 for Amber and 45 for Red. The middle half of Red loans trades between roughly 50 and 94. About $20bn of Red loans trade at distressed levels, versus none in Green.

The Green-Red price gap has widened from 17pt to 25pt this year. In CCC-rated software the gap is 40pt, up from 27pt at the start of the year. Green loans have retraced about half of their decline from the March trough. Amber and Red hit new lows in June and May respectively.

Refinancing is open but selective. 10 of 11 completed refinancing or amend-and-extend deals in software and adjacent sectors were Green or Amber. The one Red issuer, Conga, scores 50 and refinanced only on its second attempt. A&E deals extended maturities 1-3 years with spread step-ups of roughly 50-225bp, OIDs of 95-97 and tighter lender protections.

MS estimates low-B and CCC Red names would face coupon step-ups of 550-1,000bp to refinance pre-2029 maturities today. For low-B names the estimated step-up is about 100bp for Green and about 400bp for Amber.

About 75% ($30bn) of the $39bn Red cohort matures in 2027-29, versus 38% of the broader software universe. 2028-29 maturities total $90bn, of which $28bn (31%) is Red. MS argues AI risk can accelerate credit deterioration through restricted refinancing access before it shows in operating results.

Of 7 software and adjacent defaults this year, 5 were Red and 2 Amber. Defaults named are Syniverse, The Knot Worldwide, System1, Optiv, West Corp, Perforce and RSA Security. Of 22 software issuers downgraded by S&P or Moody's YTD, about half are Red, although Red is 22% of the 131-issuer universe by count. Only one downgraded issuer is Green.

MS sees risks skewing toward a better default outcome than it expected earlier this year, given the refinancings. It flags 13 issuers (10% of the 131) as facing a materially higher probability of default through year-end 2027. These are low-quality names with near-term maturities and high AI risk.

By archetype, Front Office Applications has the largest Red share at 32% of outstanding. IT & Tech-Enabled Services is bifurcated between Red and Green. Back Office (average risk score 40) and Vertical Applications (37) are the most resilient. Cybersecurity has 51% of debt maturing by 2029 and 25% distressed.

Model-implied pricing screens IT & Tech-Enabled Services rich (52% of loans more than 5pt above model) and screens Cybersecurity and Data & Infrastructure with meaningful shares cheap. Within Red, about 34% screen rich and 45% cheap. MS calls these relative-value signals rather than evidence of mispricing.

IT & Tech-Enabled Services has recovered strongly on issuer-specific events. Rackspace's $1.6bn TLB rose from 45 to 84 on repurchases, AI partnerships and a 15% headcount cut. Peraton's $5.7bn TLB rose from 84 to 91.

CLOs hold $133bn (about 54%) of the covered software loans. Their mix is 38% Green, 50% Amber and 12% Red, versus 35%, 49% and 16% for the market. CLOs hold 41% of Red loans versus 59% of Green loans.

CLO managers have rotated since February. Net buys were $2.8bn of Green and $1.2bn of Amber, and net sales were $1.1bn of Red. They sold $2.27bn of 2028 paper and $219mn of 2029, and bought $3.27bn of 2031, $1.02bn of 2030 and $959mn of 2033. The rotation can crystallize par losses.

Within CLOs, software quality mix matters more than quantity. Deals with BB MVOC below 102.5% hold 14.2% software, with Red at 14.7% of it. Deals above 105.5% hold 11.1% software, with Red at 5.4%. A 1pp rise in Red exposure goes with about 1pp lower BB MVOC (correlation -0.54), while Green shows only 0.12. The market penalizes identifiable Red exposure more than it rewards Green.

MS stays cautious down the CLO capital stack, especially mezzanine. It stresses collateral quality, manager selection and deal selection that combines AI risk with MVOC, maturity runway and valuations. Portfolios with large Red exposure and healthy MVOC may warrant scrutiny. Portfolios with low Red exposure and low MVOC may be underappreciated.

Fundamentals remain resilient. Software loan issuers posted 5% y/y EBITDA growth in 2Q26 versus 8% for the broader leveraged loan index, on a sample of only 10 issuers. Median consensus points to 6-9% EBITDA growth in 2027. AI can pressure gross margins through usage-based costs, which makes margin preservation a key differentiator for PE sponsors.

The method has stated limits. It uses only public information, does not explicitly incorporate sponsor ability, and the 35/50 band thresholds are described as somewhat arbitrary. Only 13% of the 131 issuers are public and 79% are sponsor-backed. Scores are validated against MS equity, fixed income and credit trading views.

sector_views.rationale: AI risk is concentrated in weaker credits. Refinancing is accessible for lower-risk names and constrained for Red names, and dispersion is expected to widen.

sector_views.sector: CLO mezzanine and lower capital stack
sector_views.rationale: MS remains cautious down the capital stack because dispersion in software collateral quality and manager response should drive performance tiering.

earnings_insights: Software loan issuers recorded 5% y/y EBITDA growth in 2Q26 versus 8% for the broader leveraged loan index (reported, FactSet, sample of 10 issuers). Median consensus estimates for 2027 EBITDA growth are 6-9% (estimate).
Tech sector EBITDA margin saw a 0.9% y/y decline in 2Q26 (reported, FactSet).

macro_indicators.interpretation: In-place fundamentals remain resilient, and the broader leveraged loan index grew 8%. The sample is only 10 issuers.

macro_indicators.indicator: Software loan EBITDA growth, median consensus
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus sees continued growth, so the fundamental impact of AI disruption may lie further out.

macro_indicators.indicator: Estimated coupon step-up to refinance, Red low-B/CCC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Refinancing is very costly for high-AI-risk issuers and leaves them with limited options.

trade_ideas.description: Relative-value screen: scrutinize CLO portfolios with sizable Red software exposure and healthy MVOC, since Red loans near par may reprice. Portfolios with low Red exposure and low MVOC may be underappreciated. Stay cautious down the CLO capital stack, especially mezzanine.
trade_ideas.rationale: Red loans trading near par may not reflect longer-term business-model disruption, which could erode MVOC and weigh on lower-rated CLO liabilities.
trade_ideas.risk: Collateral discounts may reflect other credit or technical factors, and AI risk scores may change over time.

risk_factors: Refinancing capacity for Red borrowers, with 75% of Red exposure maturing in 2027-29 and coupon step-ups of 550-1,000bp
Red loans still trading near par may not fully reflect longer-term disruption
Potential for greater loan price volatility as borrowers' AI management and refinancings are tested
Par erosion for CLO managers who sell discounted Red loans to buy higher-priced Green loans
Gross margin pressure from usage-based AI costs
Scores are a snapshot built on public data, and names can migrate between Amber and Red

Exhibit 37 shows Red share of software holdings of 14.7% in deals with BB MVOC below 102.5%, versus 5.4% above 105.5%.
Exhibit 21 shows current weighted-average bid, YTD low and year-end 2025 price by band: Green 97 (low 94, 3/3/2026, YE 100), Amber 88 (low 87, 6/30/2026, YE 96), Red 73 (low 71, 5/21/2026, YE 83).
Exhibit 10 shows Front Office Applications with 32% of outstanding in Red, versus 16% for the total sector.
vol_and_positioning: CLO managers have net bought Green and Amber software loans and net sold Red loans since February, and have moved out of 2028-29 maturities into 2030-33.
Red exposure has a correlation of -0.54 with BB MVOC across CLO deals. Green exposure has a correlation of 0.12.

tension_points.bull_case: Refinancing markets remain open, and defaults and A&Es have gone better than expected. Green loans have retraced about half of their March losses and CLO managers have rotated up in quality. MS sees risks skewing toward a better default outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: Red loans face 550-1,000bp coupon step-ups, and 75% of Red matures in 2027-29. Red loans still near par may not reflect longer-term disruption. 5 of 7 defaults this year were Red.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Red issuers with 2028-29 maturities failing to demonstrate earnings resilience or secure runway before returning to markets, or evidence of AI disruption appearing in reported fundamentals.

tension_points.bull_case: CLOs hold 12% Red versus 16% market-wide, and managers have rotated into Green and longer maturities.
tension_points.bear_case: Deals with more Red exposure have lower BB MVOC and wider spreads. Red loans near par could reprice and erode MVOC, which weighs on lower-rated CLO liabilities.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of disruption emerging in Red loans that trade near par.
